Optic disc malformations, macular atrophy and chorioretinal disease cause impaired vision; manifestations remain within the ocular axis.
Mitochondrial respiratory-chain disorder; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in 2/2 and encephalopathy in 1/1 reported patients. Optic atrophy frequency is unspecified.
Cortical malformations and developmental impairment define the disorder; cataract reported in 1/3 patients (~33%), although the sample is small.
Fibromatosis arises in plantar fascia; persistent skin tethering/loss of elasticity occurs in 80-99%, subcutaneous nodules in 30-79%. Neuropathy is only 5-29%.
Skeletal fusion dysplasia; enamel hypoplasia and hearing impairment each occur in 30-79%. Retinal abnormalities are rare and cataract frequency is unspecified.
Xp duplication syndromes commonly cause developmental delay or intellectual disability; other organ abnormalities vary with the duplicated segment.
RAX2-associated macular degeneration directly affects the retina and central vision.
Angelman neurodevelopmental disorder with intellectual impairment and seizures; pigmentation differences and dental spacing do not establish additional organ damage.
Carcinoma originates in sebaceous glands of the eyelid or caruncle, included in the ocular axis; metastases are not defining organ involvement.
Palmar epidermal and sweat-related disorder; cystic fibrosis and autoimmune conditions are associations, not organs directly damaged by this keratoderma.
Adenocarcinoma originates in reproductive epithelium of the rete testis; endocrine gonadal disease is not described.
Malignant neoplasm of the biliary tree; intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts belong to the hepatic axis.
Inherited macular dystrophy with vitelliform lesions in 8/8 and reduced visual acuity in 5/8 patients.
Defined by progressive basal ganglia degeneration and erythrocyte acanthocytosis; cardiomyopathy and myopathy vary across constituent disorders.
GJB2-related nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; occasional vestibular dysfunction remains within the otologic axis.
Defined as a delusional psychiatric syndrome, usually in psychosis; neurological causes in a subset do not establish intrinsic neurological damage across the concept.
Cardiomyopathy, skeletal deformity/scoliosis and optic atrophy each occur in 30-79%. Cap reached; bladder dysfunction is neurogenic, and colitis is separately diagnosed.
Familial dilated cardiomyopathy with myocardial fibrosis in 4/4 patients and frequent ventricular arrhythmias.
COL10A1-related skeletal dysplasia affecting metaphyses, limb alignment and hip development; no established common extra-skeletal damage.
Primary skeletal myopathy; dysphagia reflects swallowing-muscle weakness rather than intrinsic gastrointestinal injury. Cardiomyopathy and respiratory insufficiency occur in 5-29%.
Hepatic venous outflow obstruction directly affects vessels and liver. Congestive splenomegaly alone does not establish blood-organ dysfunction; renal injury occurs in 5-29%.
Atrophy of the lacrimal apparatus is directly within the ocular axis; no underlying systemic cause is specified.
Renal cystic disease in 18/18; hepatic cystic involvement in 15/19 (~79%) represents direct structural occupation, although liver dysfunction is only 5-29%.
Sphingomyelin storage; neurodegeneration and hepatic injury approach 100%, lung infiltration 80-99% with respiratory failure 30-79%. Haematologic damage omitted under cap.
